Can you solve the following math problem? A cow is tethered in the middle of a field with a 14 feet long rope. If the cow grazes 10 sq.ft. per day, then approximately what time will be taken by the cow to graze the whole field?. Please select your answer from the following options: A)51 days, B)61 days, C)71 days, D)81 days, E)91 days.

The area of the field can be calculated using the formula for the area of a circle: A = πr^2, where r is the length of the rope, which is 14 feet in this case. 

Therefore, the area of the field is approximately 14^2 x π ≈ 616 sq.ft. 

Since the cow grazes 10 sq.ft. per day, it will take approximately 616 sq.ft. / 10 sq.ft. per day = 61.6 days to graze the whole field. 

Rounded to the nearest whole number, the answer is 61 days. 

So, the correct answer is B) 61 days.

Since the cow is tethered in the middle of the field with a 14 feet long rope, the radius of the circle is half of the rope length, i.e., 14/2 = 7 feet.

So, the area of the circle the cow can graze in is:
A = π(7)² = 49π ≈ 153.94 sq.ft.

If the cow grazes 10 sq.ft. per day, then the time taken by the cow to graze the whole field is:
Time = Area of field / Grazing rate
Time = 153.94 / 10 = 15.394 days

Therefore, the cow will take approximately 16 days to graze the whole field.

Answer: The closest option is A) 51 days.```
